title: Daniel Thomas jailed for 15 months for slashing dinghy
originalTitle: Daniel Thomas jailed for 15 months for slashing dinghy
content:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been jailed for 15 months for slashing a dinghy with a knife in the English Channel.

The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, live-streamed himself cutting the boat while a French rescue worker was on board in September.

Sentencing him after he admitted criminal damage, a judge called Thomas a "publicity seeker" whose actions were a "flagrant interference" with the work of rescue crews.

His barrister argued it was an act of "performative activism" rather than a "political crime" and said nobody had been put in danger.

Thomas founded the anti-migrant group Patriot Platform, which was behind protests in Portsmouth and Dover involving masked men in September.

He appeared at Portsmouth Crown Court by video link from HMP Winchester, and sat with his head in his hands for much of the hearing.

The court heard he had watched migrants being taken off the dinghy by the RNLI, Border Force and the French Coastguard on 22 September, before telling those on his boat to steer towards it.

He said "let's get rid of that boat" before slashing it about eight times, the court heard.

It had previously been reported that Thomas said "this is what needs to happen to everyone in these boats" in his live-stream of the incident, but the court heard on Friday that he said "this is what needs to happen to every one of these boats".

Earlier in the footage, Thomas told viewers "no violence, nothing like that" and urged them to "share this everywhere".

He gave a postcode in Gosport, which the judge said he believed was to "encourage protest".

After slashing the boat, he shouted at the rescue worker: "Get off the boat, you've got time to get off the boat," the court heard.

Joel Smith KC, prosecuting, said it was "more a matter of luck than judgement that serious consequences did not arise".

The dinghy was later destroyed by French authorities, meaning the value of the damage could not be proven.

Judge James Newton-Price KC said it was "not for me to make any judgement of the political cause," but that the attack was "intended to have an impact on a live audience".

Commenting on the Border Force, coastguard and RNLI crews, he said: "They do necessary, highly sensitive and difficult jobs, which should not be disrupted by a publicity-seeker slashing with a knife a boat they were attempting to recover."

Simon Pentol KC, defending, said the dinghy did not sink and made its way back to France without help.

The judge accepted that prison had caused hardship for Thomas's family, including his four children. He said the sentence would have been 20 months had he gone to trial, and his time on remand would count towards it.

A separate charge of failing to give police the PIN to his phone, which Thomas denied, was ordered to lie on his file.

He is due to stand trial at Westminster Magistrates' Court in June over separate alleged offences in Dover, which he denies.
